papers.title: Type Ia-CSM Supernovae. I. Uniform Light-Curve Characterization and Inference on the Underlying Type Ia Explosions
papers.abstract: We present the largest uniform study to date of 50 thermonuclear Type Ia supernovae interacting with circumstellar medium (SNe Ia-CSM). As the first paper in a series delineating the population properties of this class, this work focuses specifically on a uniform analysis of their light curves. Our results show that SNe Ia-CSM display a significantly more uniform light-curve morphology than interacting core-collapse SNe IIn, closely resembling the luminous-slow subgroup. The Ia-CSM sample spans approximately an order of magnitude in peak luminosity, total timescale, and radiated energy, with a median optical peak luminosity of $\approx2\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$ ($\approx-20$ mag). We find a distinct bimodality in the radiated energy distribution: a predominant population of energetic events with $\approx 2\times10^{50}$ erg and characteristic timescales of $\approx100$ days, and a secondary population that is roughly an order of magnitude less energetic with shorter timescales of $\approx50$ days. Decomposition of the luminosity contributions from underlying SN Ia and CSM interaction by the Ia-CSM spectral classification reveals a diverse range of underlying SN Ia subtypes spanning from luminous 1991T-like to faint 1991bg-like. Both SN Ia and CSM properties are broadly consistent with the core-degenerate channel resulting from common-envelope evolution followed by core merger, where the presence of dense CSM is dictated by the delay time between the common-envelope phase and the thermonuclear explosion. Subsequent papers in this series will utilize numerical simulations, semi-analytical modeling, spectroscopy, and host-galaxy environments to further constrain the progenitor and explosion pathways to SNe Ia-CSM.

papers.title: A self-shadowing black hole accretion disk at sub-Eddington luminosities
papers.abstract: Accretion onto black holes powers some of the most energetic sources in the Universe, yet its behaviour across the luminosity range remains poorly understood. Specifically, as the luminosity approaches the Eddington limit ($L_{\rm Edd}$), the inner accretion disk is expected to depart from the standard thin-disk solution, becoming vertically extended. The luminosity threshold and observational signatures of this transition remain, however, uncertain. We present multiwavelength spectroscopy obtained during the decay of a black hole X-ray binary outburst. At the peak ($\sim 0.2\,L_{\rm Edd}$), a cool optical and near-infrared spectrum dominated by strong recombination lines of hydrogen and He I is observed. However, as the luminosity decreases, it switches to a hot, highly irradiated, nearly featureless spectrum. This puzzling behavior reveals the emergence of a vertically extended inner disk at the outburst peak, shielding the outer regions from high-energy radiation produced near the black hole; a scenario supported by contemporaneous X-ray spectra. Observations of similar systems suggest that this phenomenon may be common among black hole accretion disks. Self-shadowing structures at luminosities well below $L_{\rm Edd}$ have major implications for black hole accretion flows and their observational properties, affecting inferred black hole spins, X-ray polarization measurements, and the physical conditions of the outer disk and its associated outflows.

papers.title: Impact of dynamical, quadratic, and higher-order tidal effects on gravitational-wave observations of binary neutron stars
papers.abstract: Neutron-star binaries are prime gravitational-wave sources for current and next-generation detectors, and provide a unique probe for the behaviour of nuclear matter at supranuclear densities. Extracting information about this requires accurate waveform models that capture tidal effects during the late inspiral. We incorporate state-of-the-art tidal corrections into a post-Newtonian inspiral waveform, including dynamical tides and nonlinear contributions from quadratic Love numbers through eighth post-Newtonian (8PN) order. Using Bayesian model comparison, we find that these corrections can significantly affect the gravitational-wave signal, with the 8PN tidal response becoming comparable to lower-PN tidal contributions in the subsolar-mass regime. For exceptionally loud GW170817-like binaries observed by third-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope, higher-order tidal effects can be distinguished with high statistical significance, while neglecting them can introduce substantial biases in the inferred tidal deformabilities and, consequently, in constraints on the neutron-star equation of state. These corrections are particularly relevant for putative subsolar-mass binaries: the lower compactness of their constituents enhances tidal effects and makes them potentially important even for current detectors. Our results highlight the importance of higher-order tidal corrections for precision gravitational-wave measurements of dense nuclear matter.

papers.title: Revisiting the distance to 4U 1543-475 through X-ray dust-scattering rings
papers.abstract: We derived a geometrical distance of the black-hole X-ray binary 4U 1543-475 based on X-ray dust-scattering rings associated with its 1992 and 2002 outbursts. We analyzed archival ROSAT and XMM-Newton observations and identified an X-ray dust-scattering ring in each observation, produced by two different dust layers along the line of sight. By combining the angular radii of the rings with the independently determined distances of the scattering dust layers and the epochs of the corresponding outbursts, we derive a best-constrained distance to 4U 1543-475 of 4.6 $\pm$ 0.2 kpc. This value is substantially smaller than the distance of 7.5 kpc commonly adopted in the literature and has important implications for the inferred physical properties of the system. In particular, the revised distance favors the presence of a low-mass extended-horizontal-branch donor star over a main-sequence star, calling for a reassessment of the dynamical parameters of the binary and, consequently, of the black-hole mass. The smaller distance also affects the inferred properties of the relativistic jet and the estimate of black-hole spin derived from the spectral continuum-fitting.

papers.title: Natal Kicks of Compact Binaries: I. Population Synthesis Framework and Illustrative Examples
papers.abstract: The natal kicks imparted to neutron stars and black holes at birth are critical for understanding massive-star evolution, compact-object formation, and compact binary merger rates. However, constraining these kicks is challenging, since they cannot be directly observed. Here, we outline a framework for inferring natal kick probability distributions for compact binaries. Our method embeds the rapid binary-population code COSMIC in a Monte-Carlo workflow that evolves ensembles of simulated binaries. From those which host compact objects, we can select subsets that match the observational characteristics of any given system (e.g. component masses, orbital period, mass-transfer status, systemic velocity). As a proof-of-concept, we apply this framework to six compact binaries spanning a wide range of companion masses and compact-object types. For each system, we identify the evolutionary channel(s) that could have led to the current observational characteristics, and isolate regions of allowed natal kicks and progenitor parameter space. We reconfirm that at least one black hole system, XTE J1118+480, must have received a natal kick $v_{\rm NK} > 100$ km s$^{-1}$. The neutron-star system, GX 301-2, is also inferred to have received an impulsive kick exceeding 280 km s$^{-1}$. We discuss the strengths and limitations associated with population-synthesis-based inference methods and explore the effects of adopting different prescriptions for critical binary evolution phases. We provide a detailed demonstration of the non-linear relationship between $v_{\rm NK}$ and $v_{\rm sys}$, highlighting the shortcomings of relying on observations alone to measure natal kicks. The inferred kick velocity distributions across our benchmark sample are generally consistent with previous constraints.

papers.title: Natal Kicks of Compact Binaries: II. Neutron-star and black-hole systems share similar kick distributions
papers.abstract: Natal kicks - kinematic impulses to neutron stars and black holes at birth - play a decisive role in the end-stage evolution of binaries hosting massive stars, in determining the global phase-space properties of compact objects, and in setting expected merger-rates detectable through gravitational-wave observations. Inferring the kick ($v_{\rm NK}$) for individual systems requires well constrained binary system properties and centre-of-mass kinematics, which must then be modelled to constrain likely system characteristics at supernova. As a result, population-wide studies of kicks remain few and far between. Here, we model plausible evolutionary histories for 68 accreting binaries, encompassing almost all black-hole and neutron-star X-ray binaries with 3D kinematics measurements, constraining allowed $v_{\rm NK}$ distributions for each source using a simulation framework presented in our previous paper. The resultant $v_{\rm NK}$ distribution for the sample can be simply represented by a broad Gamma distribution with mean $v_{\rm NK}$ = $128^{+17}_{-15}$ km s$^{-1}$ and scatter $\sigma$ = 117 km s$^{-1}$. Intriguingly, the distributions for black-hole vs. neutron-star systems are found to be formally indistinguishable. Despite still being limited by small-number statistics, we find that black holes can receive large natal kicks, and that kicks for all remnant types span similar ranges (0-700 km s$^{-1}$). There is a hint, but no statistically significant evidence at present, for $v_{\rm NK}$ scaling inversely with black-hole mass. Our work suggests either that similar physics drives kicks and shows evidence for effects beyond simplistic fallback-moderated scaling for black holes, or that selection effects conspire to erase differences between remnant types in current accreting-binary samples. Larger samples are needed to provide robust discriminatory tests between these possibilities.

papers.title: General Relativistic and Non-Inertial Effects on Magnetic Reconnection Rates
papers.abstract: We develop a gauge-independent theory of magnetic reconnection beyond the standard special-relativistic framework of inertial systems in flat spacetime. Our definitions of reconnection and its rate are independent of reference frame and coordinate system, allowing physical effects of gravity and net linear acceleration to be distinguished from coordinate effects. We extend the mesoscale theory of Liu et al. [PRL 118, 085101 (2017)], in which the reconnection rate depends on physics both within the diffusion region and in an upstream ideal, force-free region. The theory identifies three non-inertial and curved-spacetime (NICS) effects, including gravitationally induced magnetic tension: gravitational distortion of the reconnection plane changes the curvature of magnetic field lines. Applying the theory to a simplified accretion plasma near )a compact object, we find that (1) whether gravity increases or decreases the reconnection rate depends on the system's orientation relative to the gravitational source, with the greatest increase occurring when the outflow jet points toward or away from the source; and (2) the magnitude of the gravitational effect scales with the dimensionless parameter $\bar{\kappa} \equiv r_s\Delta y^2/r^3$, where $r$ is the Schwarzschild radial coordinate, $r_s$ is the source's Schwarzschild radius, and $\Delta y$ is the mesoscale length.

papers.title: A faint thermonuclear X-ray burst from SAX~J1808.4--3658 observed with NICER: possible evidence for burst-driven changes in the inner disk structure
papers.abstract: We present spectral and temporal properties of a faint thermonuclear X-ray burst observed from SAX~J1808.4--3658 by NICER. Unlike the previous analysis of the same burst \citep{2023ApJ...948..117C}, our analysis focuses on the persistent spectral evolution and changes in the accretion environment. Following a peak flux of approximately 5\% of the Eddington limit, the burst emission settled into a stable state characterized by a temperature of 0.46 keV and a flux 14\% greater than the pre-burst value in the tail. Although the observation was truncated, it resumed after 3 hours, revealing that the source flux returned to its pre-burst level. Our spectral fitting results indicate that at the peak of the burst, the neutron star's surface emission was fully exposed, subsequently becoming increasingly obscured while remaining above the pre-burst emission. Fitting the persistent spectra also reveals an increase in the visible fraction of the neutron star's surface from 25\% to 41\% during the period from 100 s to 550 s after the burst, suggesting a change in the disk structure (the height or the inner radius). The spectral evolution suggests a transient reorganization of the inner accretion flow during the burst peak, followed by partial recovery as the burst flux declines.

papers.title: Revisiting the Neutrino Emission and Physical Parameter Constraints from Time-Resolved Spectra of Gamma-Ray Bursts
papers.abstract: The non-detection of neutrinos associated with gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) has placed significant constraints on the physical parameter space of GRB jet models. However, most of these constraints have been derived using the time-integrated spectra. In this paper, we adopt time-resolved spectra, which provide a more detailed description of the prompt emission spectral structure, to calculate the neutrino emission, and investigate how they affect the constraints on GRB physical parameters. By selecting three GRBs (i.e., GRBs 090902B, 110721A and 080916C) whose spectra are composed of different components (e.g., thermal, thermal + non-thermal, and non-thermal), we find that the expected neutrino event numbers from the summed time-resolved spectra are lower than those from the time-integrated approach in the region of relatively low dissipation radius $R$ and bulk Lorentz factor $\Gamma$, while the opposite trend is found at high $R$ and high $\Gamma$. Moreover, we also use GECAM-C data to calculate the neutrino emission of the brightest GRB 221009A, and find that the expected number of neutrino events calculated from the summed time-resolved spectra is approximately three times that from the time-integrated spectra in the high-$R$ and high-$\Gamma$ regime. More details of constraints on the physical parameters are also discussed. These results highlight the importance of time-resolved spectra for future GRB neutrino studies.

papers.title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
papers.abstract: Supermassive neutron stars ($M \gtrsim 2\ M_{\odot}$) provide stringent constraints on the equation of state of dense matter. We report the discovery of a wide binary system composed of a red giant star and an invisible companion with an orbital period $P\approx 1218\pm3$ days and a comparatively low eccentricity $e\approx 0.09\pm0.01$ (with $1 \sigma$ uncertainty). By combining radial velocity measurements from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) with astrometric data from {\it Gaia} DR2 and DR3 catalogues, we derive a Keplerian orbit with an inclination angle $i\approx73^{\circ}\pm11^{\circ}$. The unseen companion has a mass in the range of 1.8--2.8 $M_{\odot}$ (spanning the full spread of all estimates), with a best-fit value of $2.20^{+0.14}_{-0.13}$ $M_{\odot}$. This potentially places the unseen companion within the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. Spectral disentangling using high-resolution near-infrared APOGEE spectra shows no absorption features from an additional component, suggesting the presence of a compact object: either a supermassive neutron star or a low-mass black hole. The wide, low-eccentricity orbit is difficult to explain through standard binary evolution channels, pointing to the need for improved theoretical models to account for such systems.

papers.title: Fast Radio Burst Population Constrained by Source-Count Growth and Burst Clustering
papers.abstract: Whether all fast radio burst (FRB) sources repeat, or whether some produce only a single burst, remains an open question. Using 3,950 bursts from the CHIME/FRB Catalog 2, we measure how the numbers of apparently single and repeating sources change with observing time, correcting for the declination-dependent, beam-weighted exposure and possible variations in the detection rate. Both source counts increase approximately linearly over 300--44,000~hr, as $N_{\rm s}\propto\Delta t^{0.98\pm0.02}$ for single sources and $N_{\rm r}\propto\Delta t^{1.06\pm0.14}$ for repeaters. Consequently, the observed repeater fraction remains nearly constant at $2.6^{+0.4}_{-0.6}\%$. We interpret these results using population models that account for a distribution of detected burst rates and temporal clustering. The source counts are reproduced by a population spanning a range of rates, including sources expected to produce approximately one detectable burst over the observing time. Its detected burst rates follow a distribution close to $r^{-2}$ over 0.01--1.5~hr$^{-1}$. The burst timing and burst multiplicities provide additional constraints. Among 77 repeaters, only 6 have their first two detected bursts within a single CHIME transit, the median interval between them is 101 days, and 31 of the 52 repeaters with at least three bursts have five or more. These observations support this population and favor moderately clustered emission (Weibull shape $k\simeq0.5$) and active phases lasting months to about a year. Our results are consistent with both a single population of repeaters whose rate distribution steepens below the range probed by CHIME and a mixed population that includes genuinely one-off sources. Thus, the current data do not require a one-off population, but cannot exclude one. Longer observing baselines are needed to distinguish these possibilities.

papers.title: Detection of 2 MeV spectral bump and ~40 MeV emission line from GRB 221009A
papers.abstract: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are the most energetic transients in the Universe, but prompt MeV--sub-GeV observations remain challenging with current gamma-ray observatories. Here, using unsaturated HEPP-H measurements on board CSES-01 and cross-calibrating with likewise unsaturated GECAM-C data, we reconstruct the continuous spectral evolution of GRB 221009A over 2--255 MeV. We identify an unusual spectral bump at $\sim$2 MeV in the first light-curve peak. We also confirm a narrow emission line whose energy decreases from $\sim$40 MeV following a $t^{-1}$ evolution, and whose flux shows a ``rise-then-fall'' profile, implying weak emission from the central jet. These findings hint that a magnetically dominated, central-empty jet exists in the BOAT.

papers.title: Cosmic Ray Reacceleration and Gamma-Ray Emission via the Cloud-Wind Interaction in the Galactic Halo
papers.abstract: The interaction between cosmic rays (CRs) and multiphase gas in the Galactic halo may play an important role in shaping the hard gamma-ray spectrum of the Fermi bubbles. We investigate the interaction between a hot Galactic wind and a cold, dense gas clump with a relative velocity of $300\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$ using two-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations coupled with momentum-dependent CR transport. The system produces a bow shock and wind reacceleration region downstream, where the wind flow is faster than the initial velocity. For a CR pressure comparable to the gas pressure (CR-rich), the wind acceleration and turbulence behind the clump are enhanced. When CR pressure is dynamically weak, strong gas compression leads to significant CR spectral hardening. In contrast, for the CR-rich case, CR pressure gradients weaken the gas compression and suppress further CR reacceleration. We estimate the gamma-ray intensity from CRs, and find that reaccelerated CRs penetrate the dense clump and enhance hadronic gamma-ray emission. The gamma-ray intensity reaches $\sim 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,sr^{-1}}$ in the 1--10 GeV band, and the gamma-ray spectra become significantly harder, consistent with the Fermi bubbles' emission. These results suggest that an ensemble of dense gas clumps interacting with the Galactic wind may contribute to the gamma-ray emission of the Fermi bubbles.

papers.title: On the MeV Nuclear De-excitation Line Emission from the Vela Supernova Remnant Region
papers.abstract: We investigate the potential nuclear de-excitation $\gamma$-ray line emission from low-energy cosmic rays (LECRs) in the Vela SNR region, one of the nearest and most angularly extended core-collapse supernova remnant (SNR) complexes. We calculate the MeV line emission from Vela, Vela Jr., and Puppis A using the TALYS nuclear reaction code, considering both direct and inverse interactions between the accelerated particles and the nuclei interior to the SNRs. The proton spectra are constrained by GeV--TeV $\gamma$-ray observations under the hadronic assumption, while a broad range of spectral indices is explored to account for the poorly constrained LECR population. We find that Vela dominates the predicted line flux among the three SNRs. The integrated fluxes of the prominent 1.63 MeV $^{20}$Ne, 4.44 MeV $^{12}$C and 6.13 MeV $^{16}$O lines are approximately $1.3\times10^{-10}$ -- $1.2\times10^{-6}$, $3.2\times10^{-10}$ -- $5.6\times10^{-7}$ and $1.6\times10^{-10}$--$2.6\times10^{-7}$ $\rm ph\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}$, respectively, over the explored proton spectra. We compare the predicted line emission with both the diffuse Galactic MeV continuum and local source-related continuum emission. In our background estimate, diffuse Galactic emission is the dominant component, while inverse Compton emission from pulsar wind nebula Vela X constitutes an additional local continuum component. The relatively low diffuse background toward Vela compared with the Galactic Center makes this region a promising target for future MeV $\gamma$-ray observations. Such observations could provide direct constraints on the LECR population and particle acceleration in this complex SNR region.

papers.title: Magnetically Deformed Neutron Stars and Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: We study the geometric figures of neutron stars and magnetars with spin periods from milliseconds to seconds and magnetic fields from $10^{12}$-$10^{15}$ G to hypothetical values near the Chandrasekhar-Fermi virial scale, $10^{18}$ G. In Newtonian theory, we find the equilibrium figure of a rotating incompressible fluid with a current-free uniform interior magnetic field matched to an exterior dipole field by surface currents. For aligned axes, an oblate spheroid is obtained by minimizing the total gravitational, rotational and magnetic energy at fixed mass, volume, angular momentum and frozen magnetic flux. Its ellipticity is the sum of rotational and magnetic contributions, recovers the Ferraro limit for a weak magnetic field, and has a magnetic weight that depends on the eccentricity for large deformation. For misaligned magnetic and spin axes, we introduce a quadrupolar shape tensor and diagonalize it to find a triaxial ellipsoid whose principal axes are tilted by magnetic pressure. The tilt angle and eccentricities are computed analytically as functions of the rotational and magnetic eccentricities and the misalignment angle. The magnetic energy of the misaligned configuration is obtained in closed form in oblate spheroidal harmonics for arbitrary eccentricity and obliquity. Its weak-field deformation, up to $10^{15}$ G, is proportional to $P_2(\cos\alpha)$, which fixes the magnetic forcing tensor, and its finite-eccentricity form gives a generalized Ferraro-Maclaurin relation for rotation-dominated misaligned stars. In the weak-field regime, the triaxial eccentricity is determined by the Ferraro eccentricity and the harmonic mean of order 2 of the rotational and magnetic eccentricities. The deformation parameters give the quadrupole moments and hence the continuous gravitational-wave amplitudes, luminosity and spin-down torque of the triaxial configuration.

papers.title: What stands behind luminosity peak of type IIP supernovae?
papers.abstract: We explore the origin of an initial broad luminosity peak that precedes the light curve plateau in type IIP supernovae. It is well known that the explosion of an evolutionary red supergiant model in the frame of radiation hydrodynamics fails to reproduce the initial luminosity peak. A common practice to compensate this drawback is to introduce massive (> 0.3 Msun) circumstellar shell attached to the evolutionary model. This remedy, however, has a negative side effect - a strong deceleration of the outer ejecta, which is inconsistent with early spectral data. An alternative way out suggests modification of a hydrogen envelope of the evolutionary red supergiant model - the outer layers should have steeper density gradient. We perform the search for the optimal multi-parameter hydrodynamic model of type IIP SN 1999em based on the Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling. The major result is that the initial luminous peak is well reproduced by the explosion of the red supergiant with the logarithmic density gradient smaller than -3 in the outer layers of about 0.9 Msun. We suggest that the mechanism for the density steepening in the hydrogen envelope is closely related to the unknown mechanism responsible for the creation of the ubiquitous low-mass (< 0.01 Msun) dense confined shell detected in type IIP supernovae.

papers.title: Energetic Particle Confinement In Black Hole Accretion Disks
papers.abstract: Using tracer particles propagating in the environment provided by general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations, this paper addresses fundamental questions related to the confinement and acceleration properties in accretion disks around compact objects. By varying the spin parameter of the central black hole and the accretion regime of the disk, a comprehensive picture is obtained for particles whose Larmor radius is comparable to the gravitational radius of the system. It is found that such particles can escape the system at the outermost boundary of the simulations, though, depending on the accretion regime, the time it takes them to escape, and the energetic dynamics along the trajectory can vary significantly. Dynamics near the black hole are even more sensitive to environmental details as black holes with higher spin values generate stronger magnetic fields, which influence particle motion in non-trivial ways. The primary acceleration mechanism is identified as turbulent scattering, with the jet-sheath emerging as the dominant site for particle energization

papers.title: Origin of the Fe K$\alpha$ red excess in IC 4329A with XRISM and multi-wavelength spectroscopy
papers.abstract: We present high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy of the bright local Seyfert 1 galaxy IC 4329A obtained with \textit{XRISM}/Resolve, supported by simultaneous \textit{NuSTAR} data and quasi-simultaneous optical/near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy. Resolve separates the Fe K$\alpha$ line into a narrow core and a broad component exhibiting a red excess. We examined three scenarios for this red excess: (1) a redshifted X-ray broad line region (xBLR), (2) relativistic disk reflection, and (3) an unshifted xBLR partially absorbed by a mildly ionized absorber. All three models reproduce the X-ray spectra equally well. Our optical (H$\beta$) and NIR (Pa$\beta$) spectroscopy shows that the broad lines are redshifted by $v \sim +640\text{--}1050\text{ km s}^{-1}$, close to the solution of the redshifted xBLR model ($v_{\rm shift} = +1700_{-800}^{+1700}\text{ km s}^{-1}$). Motivated by this, we constructed a hybrid model in which the xBLR shares the velocity structure of the optical/NIR BLR and the remaining red excess is attributed to a relativistic disk line, which also provides an acceptable fit. The inferred xBLR radius is $R_{\rm BLR} \sim (3\text{--}6) \times 10^3\ R_g$ ($\sim 12\text{--}22$ light-days). From the narrow Fe K$\alpha$ core in the hybrid model (${\rm FWHM} = 870_{-280}^{+260}\text{ km s}^{-1}$), we estimate a torus distance of $R_{\rm torus} \sim 0.9_{-0.4}^{+1.0}$ pc ($\sim 1100$ light-days), close to the dust sublimation radius. Furthermore, two ultra-fast outflow (UFO) absorption features are identified with $v_{\text{wind}} \sim -0.30c$ and $-0.24c$, both confirmed at $>99\%$ confidence.

papers.title: LHAASO's Peanut source is a laboratory for studying magnetic fields in the Milky Way
papers.abstract: Recently, the LHAASO Collaboration reported gamma-ray emission from the Peanut-shaped source (Peanut), which extends over $4.5^\circ$ parallel to the Galactic plane at $b=-17.5^\circ$. The source is associated with the millisecond pulsar PSR J0218+4232, located at the eastern edge of the Peanut, at a distance of 3 kpc from the Earth and 0.9 kpc from the Galactic plane. Its location and bright gamma-ray emission above 25 TeV make it a natural laboratory for studying the Galactic magnetic field (GMF) in the transition region between the Galactic plane and halo. We interpret the observed emission as inverse-Compton scattering of CMB photons by electrons propagating along the large-scale GMF, accounting for turbulence through two models: Kolmogorov and Goldreich-Sridhar (GS). These models correspond to diffusive and ballistic particle propagation, respectively. While the GS case naturally provides conditions for one-sided gamma-ray emission, in the Kolmogorov case assumptions of one-sided particle injection and magnetic mirror at the source are necessary. We find that, in the Kolmogorov scenario, the Peanut's hotspots are likely associated with magnetic bottling, whereas in the GS scenario, they are related to magnetic field line geometry. Both models yield constraints on the GMF at the location of the Peanut.

papers.title: Search for gravitational wave coincident neutrinos in DEAP-3600
papers.abstract: We searched DEAP-3600 data for neutrino signals coincident with gravitational waves from compact object mergers observed by the LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA collaborations (LVK). While mergers involving neutron stars are expected to produce neutrinos, these have never been detected. The DEAP-3600 experiment is sensitive to electron neutrinos as recently observed through charged current neutrino absorption on its $^{40}$Ar target. Between 2016 and 2020, the detector recorded data during seven compact merger events involving neutron stars that were observed gravitationally by LVK. Upon examination, there is no statistically significant evidence of neutrinos from any of the mergers analyzed. Exclusion limits are set on the electron neutrino fluence, e.g. from GW170817 in the mono-energetic model at $6.8\times10^{12}~\text{cm$^{-2}$}$ ($1.8\times10^{10}~\text{cm$^{-2}$}$) for 10 MeV (100 MeV) neutrinos.

papers.title: Frequency-dependent time delays in Sgr A* from a broadband VLA observation
papers.abstract: Frequency-dependent radio time delays have been measured in Sgr A* light curves, with higher-frequency emission generally leading lower-frequency emission. These lags have been interpreted in terms of an organized jet-like outflow, expanding plasma components, or magnetic-flux eruptions, although their origin and recurrence remain uncertain. We aim to search for and quantify frequency-dependent radio time delays in a new high-cadence Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) observation of Sgr A*. Using the improved broad 12-37 GHz frequency coverage, we measured the timing of the dominant variability feature and compared the resulting lag-wavelength slope with previous measurements. Sgr A* was observed with the VLA on 28 May 2022 in the Ku, K, and Ka bands over a 6-hour track. We extracted both band-averaged and 2 GHz subband light curves and measured the delays using a peak-time method and a locally normalized cross-correlation function. The light curves show one broad variability feature, with the maximum occurring progressively later at lower observing frequencies. Both timing methods recover a positive lag-wavelength relation, with a slope of order 40 min/cm. This value agrees with time lag results reported over more than 15 years from the first VLA observations at 22-43 GHz to later multifrequency VLA and ALMA campaigns. The sign and magnitude of the estimated delay are consistent with outward propagation through an optically thick synchrotron-emitting region. The recurrence of comparable delays over almost two decades suggests that frequency-dependent radio lags are a persistent feature of Sgr A* variability. Broadband, multi-epoch VLA monitoring of Sgr A* provides a useful probe of its radio variability, but robust lag measurements require high cadence and improved (u,v) coverage of both Sgr A* and the surrounding extended emission such as by combining different VLA configurations.

papers.title: Rebrightening in the Radio: Secondary Flares from Tidal Disruption Events AT2019ehz and AT2019eve
papers.abstract: We present the discovery of new secondary delayed radio flares from two tidal disruption events (TDEs), AT2019ehz and AT2019eve from observations ranging 1-18 GHz using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array. For AT2019ehz, we find a secondary flare in radio emission began at 1545 days post-disruption, 770 days after the first radio flare detected at 775 days post-disruption, and for AT2019eve the secondary flare was detected at 1594 days post-disruption, 825 days after its initial radio detection at 769 days post-disruption. Through spectral modeling of the multi-frequency observations, we extract physical parameters of the new flares to constrain the origin of the rebrightening. We find the secondary flare of AT2019ehz is likely produced by a second outflow launched at roughly 1000 days. For AT2019eve, the secondary flare reveals unexpected spectral evolution with a self-absorbed peak increasing from 1325 to 2173 days post-disruption, which is not well explained with most models of expanding outflows and instead suggests a more complex physical geometry. This inconclusive origin of AT2019eve highlights the need for more complex models to explain observed TDE radio evolution.

papers.title: Self-Regulated Cosmic-Ray Electron Acceleration in High-Mach-Number MHD-PIC Shocks
papers.abstract: Shock waves in supernova remnants are thought to accelerate cosmic rays (CRs) via diffusive shock acceleration (DSA). If acceleration is efficient, CR-modified shock models and nonlinear DSA predict smoothly decelerated precursors and concave spectra that harden with energy. These predictions are in tension with observations, which favor spectra closer to the test-particle form, $4 \pi f(p) p^{4} = {\rm const}$ or steeper. We use one- and two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic-particle-in-cell simulations to follow the long-term nonlinear coupling of the thermal plasma and CR electrons in non-relativistic quasi-parallel, high-Mach-number shocks. We choose electrons over ions for their larger charge per unit mass, probing the limits of current-driven feedback. We vary the supplied CR-electron mass fraction to measure the shock's response. Our injection model determines the effective injection and acceleration from particle trajectories through the evolving upstream turbulence, rather than a prescribed shock injection fraction. The reflected CR-electron current excites Bell-type non-resonant turbulence. The resulting magnetic structures scatter and isotropize the current-carrying particles, limiting the coherent upstream current and suppressing the formation of a spatially extended CR-pressure precursor. Across the CR-electron mass supply explored, the saturated upstream magnetic energy and far-upstream CR current converge to similar levels. In 1D, the downstream high-energy spectrum approaches the test-particle DSA shape across the resolved momentum range, with nonthermal pressure reaching a few tens of percent of the upstream ram pressure. These results suggest that, once injection is sufficient to sustain strong current-driven turbulence, supernova-remnant shocks can approach a common regulated state largely insensitive to the details of CR injection.

papers.title: An analytic diffusion model for viewing-angle effects in explosive transients
papers.abstract: The tight observed relation between the peak bolometric luminosity, $L_{\mathrm p}$, and the width ratio $L_{30}/L_{\mathrm p}$ of Type Ia supernovae, with $L_{30}$ the luminosity 30 d after explosion, makes viewing-angle effects a useful test of explosion models. We develop an analytic diffusion model for homologously expanding asymmetric ejecta with uniform density and grey opacity, based on a Green's-function solution and an Eddington surface-emission prescription, and obtain angle-dependent light curves for a displaced spherical source and for oblate ejecta. We validate them against Monte Carlo (MC) radiative transfer and derive geometric approximations to the peak-luminosity anisotropy. For a displaced spherical source, the quasi-steady approximation, equivalent to stationary diffusion in frozen ejecta, gives $L_{\mathrm p}(\theta)/L_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{avg}}\simeq1+(17/8)z_{\mathrm{off}}\cos\theta$, where $z_{\mathrm{off}}$ is the displacement in units of the ejecta radius, $\theta$ the viewing angle from the displacement axis, and $L_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{avg}}$ the angle-averaged peak. This dipole is $\mathord{\approx}10$ per cent below the finite-time value in the tested configurations. For oblate ejecta, the leading term is quadrupolar and is set by a single shape parameter. Effective models of 19 off-centre sub-Chandrasekhar explosions recover the MC peak times, peak luminosities, and width ratios to median errors of 3, 4, and 6 per cent, and the extent in $L_{\mathrm p}$ of the MC tracks, but underestimate the width-ratio variation with viewing angle by a factor of 2 to 3. An oblate construction captures the scale of peak luminosity variations in six equal-mass white-dwarf collisions. The model tracks remain inconsistent with the observed distribution, and for asymmetric models the transverse viewing-angle variation adds to the tension.

papers.title: PSR J1807-2459B in NGC 6544: A Unique Relativistic Binary in a Dense Cluster
papers.abstract: The globular cluster NGC 6544 is a high-density, dynamically evolved system located in the direction of the Galactic Center, known for hosting the eccentric binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1807-2459B. We present a new timing solution for this pulsar, based on more than 26 years of observations with the Parkes, Green Bank and MeerKAT radio telescopes. We measure for the first time the variation of the orbital period, which is dominated by the acceleration of the binary in the cluster potential: this places the pulsar in front of the cluster center and reveals its intrinsic spin-down, typical of a fully recycled millisecond pulsar. We also improve the measurements of the rate of advance of periastron and of the Einstein delay, the latter by a factor of four, and include the previously neglected contributions of the proper motion, which makes these parameters and the derived masses of the pulsar and its companion, $1.3636^{+0.0017}_{-0.0021}\,M_\odot$ and $1.2071^{+0.0021}_{-0.0017}\,M_\odot$, more realistic. Together with the Shapiro delay, these measurements allow two independent tests of general relativity, both passed. Our results show that precise post-Keplerian parameters of a binary pulsar in a dense cluster can probe both the cluster gravitational field and general relativity, provided that kinematic effects are carefully taken into account.

papers.title: Hump around 30 keV in Suzaku spectra of Aquila X-1 -- Possible evidence of strong rapid-proton capture process --
papers.abstract: In a neutron star low-mass X-ray binary, heavy elements (with mass number ~100) are believed to be synthesized through the rapid-proton (rp) capture process, as indirectly indicated by the long tail of X-ray burst light curves. Although direct evidence for the rp-process was lacking so far, we reported in our previous study that an unidentified hump is present at ~30 keV of the Suzaku spectra of Aquila X-1 in its hard state. The feature was tentatively identified with a recombination quasi-continuum from highly ionized ions of cadmium or indium, which are possibly produced by the rp process during X-ray bursts and lifted up into the neutron-star atmosphere. To reinforce this scenario, we quantitatively evaluated the physical conditions of the assumed emitting region in the atmosphere, and confirmed that the scenario is possible when the putative rp-process ashes in the atmosphere has ~10^7 times higher abundances than their solar values. The results are compared with theoretical model calculations for the nucleosynthesis in X-ray bursts. We suggest that the observed spectral hump is a radiative recombination feature from the stable isotope 106Cd, produced in X-ray bursts via the rp-process. Further issues about the detectability are briefly discussed.

papers.title: What the X-ray Emission from Young Supernovae Can Tell Us About Their Progenitors
papers.abstract: We discuss constraints that the X-ray emission from supernovae can place on their progenitor stars. Since almost all X-ray supernovae arise from massive stars, we concentrate on implications for massive stars. These stars lose mass throughout their lifetime in the form of stellar winds. X-ray emission can be used to gauge the wind properties, especially the mass-loss rates, via various techniques. The abundance of various elements formed by nucleosynthesis within the stars, and released in the stellar explosion, can be estimated from X-ray spectra. In many cases, a combination of X-ray light curves and spectra can allow us to extricate the structure and morphology of the surrounding medium formed by pre-supernova mass loss into which the SN shock is expanding.

papers.title: Jet energetics and remnant magnetism in short gamma-ray bursts from binary neutron-star mergers: A statistical study via broadband afterglow modeling
papers.abstract: Short gamma-ray bursts (sGRBs) are believed to originate from compact binary mergers, particularly binary neutron star (BNS) mergers, providing a probe of jet energetics and merger remnants. We compile broadband afterglow observations of 40 sGRBs and perform forward-shock modeling with off-axis Gaussian jets, excluding data potentially affected by additional energy injection. We derive distributions of beaming-corrected jet kinetic energy $E_k$ and radiative efficiency $\eta_\gamma$, and combine these with binary population synthesis and numerical simulations to infer remnant black hole (BH) magnetic fields assuming the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) jet-launching mechanism. For the 15 strictly constrained bursts, we find a median $E_k\simeq3.8\times10^{49}$ erg and $\eta_\gamma\simeq0.35$, with respective 68% intervals of $[5.1\times10^{48},1.9\times10^{50}]$ erg and [0.09, 0.79]. The inferred magnetic field supplied by the accretion disk and threading the BH horizon is approximately $7\times10^{15}$ G, with a 68% credible interval of $[2.3\times10^{15},2.4\times10^{16}]$ G, depending slightly on the neutron star equation of state. The full sample yields a higher median field of approximately $2\times10^{16}$ G, with the high-energy and high-field tails predominantly contributed by less well-constrained bursts. These results provide statistical constraints on sGRB jet energetics and suggest characteristic BH magnetic fields of order $10^{16}$ G. Comparison with pre-merger neutron star magnetic fields indicates a characteristic amplification factor of $\eta_B\sim10^3$, providing an observational constraint on magnetic field amplification during BNS mergers and subsequent BH formation.

papers.title: 3D radiative transfer of K-series lines of He-like ions with SKIRT
papers.abstract: High-resolution X-ray spectroscopy with XRISM has resolved line profiles of highly ionised ions, including P Cygni profiles, in many systems containing compact objects. To interpret these line profiles, forward modelling with three-dimensional radiative transfer (3D RT) calculations including the relevant ionic processes is required. Following our previous work on the Lyman-series lines of H-like ions, we present the implementation of the K-series lines of He-like ions with Z = 2-30 in the open-source Monte Carlo RT code SKIRT, providing a numerical tool for interpreting highresolution X-ray spectra of photoionised plasmas. Building upon the framework developed for H-like ions, we incorporate the resonance scattering (RS) and radiative recombination (RR) channels. We also implement the inner-shell ionisation (II) channel of Li-like ions for the production of He-like lines. We resolve fine-structure levels and account for level populations, frequency redistribution, phase function, and linear polarisation through transition-specific Mueller matrices. The implementation reproduces the expected RT effects in He-like lines. The Fe xxv w and y lines, dominated by the RS channel, develop optically thick line-profile distortions and P Cygni profiles in an outflowing plasma, whereas the x and z lines, dominated by the RR and II channels, do not exhibit such behaviour. The line intensities from the RS and RR channels agree well with Cloudy. The II channel further enhances the z line, which is not yet included in Cloudy. The linear polarisation calculations reproduce the analytical and experimental angular dependence of resonance scattering on a line-by-line basis. This extension to He-like lines, together with our previous implementation of H-like lines, enables 3D RT modelling of the major X-ray lines, providing a tool for constraining gas kinematics around compact objects observed with XRISM.

papers.title: EP250226a: A fast X-ray transient associated with GRB 250226A and its multiwavelength afterglow properties
papers.abstract: Recent advances in fast X-ray transient studies have been driven by the wide-field, sensitive soft X-ray monitoring capabilities of the Einstein Probe (EP), enabling the prompt detection and localization of previously underexplored events. EP observations offer new opportunities to investigate the origins, emission mechanisms, and population properties of newly discovered fast X-ray transients. We present multiwavelength observations of EP250226a, an extragalactic fast X-ray transient associated with GRB 250226A. We jointly analyze the prompt emission from soft X-rays to gamma rays and the X-ray afterglow spectra. We collect optical photometric data, perform empirical and afterglow model-based analyses, and present optical-to-infrared spectroscopy, measuring the equivalent widths of absorption lines. The spectroscopic redshift is $z = 3.314$, and the isotropic-equivalent gamma-ray energy is $E_\mathrm{iso}\simeq7.32\times10^{53}$ erg. Its location in the Amati diagram is consistent with a massive-star core-collapse origin (Type II GRB). The fluence ratio $\rm{S}(25-50\,\rm{keV})/\rm{S}(50-100\,\rm{keV})=0.57\pm0.06$ supports its classification as a classical GRB. The X-ray and optical afterglows show achromatic behavior. Among the models considered, a top-hat jet propagating into a uniform interstellar medium best describes the multiwavelength afterglow. This model suggests a highly collimated, nearly on-axis jet, with an isotropic-equivalent kinetic energy of $E_\mathrm{k,iso}\simeq4.07\times10^{55}$ erg, a gamma-ray radiative efficiency of $\eta_{\gamma}\simeq 1.77\%$, and a low magnetic-field energy fraction of $\log \epsilon_\mathrm{B,FS} \simeq -6.52$. EP250226a exhibits typical long-duration GRB properties, with the first soft X-ray peak coinciding with the gamma-ray prompt emission, while the soft X-ray emission lasts significantly longer than the gamma-ray emission.

papers.title: Polarized transport in a Thomson slab: Stokes recursion, asymptotic eigenmodes, and Comptonization applications
papers.abstract: We develop a scattering-order-resolved Stokes-vector recursion for axisymmetric polarized transport in a finite plane-parallel Thomson slab. The post-scattering radiation field closes exactly within two depth-dependent coefficients, yielding escape probabilities, angular distributions and linear polarization while conserving photon number. At high scattering orders, the principal eigenmode of the weighted self-adjoint transport operator controls the escape statistics, and the normalized angular distribution and polarization become independent of the seed source. The subdominant spectrum quantifies convergence, with the characteristic scattering order scaling as the square of the optical depth in thick slabs. We derive logarithmic corrections to the thin-slab complete-polarization limit away from the slab normal, together with a finite-optical-depth Galerkin approximation. In optically thick slabs, matching bulk diffusion to a polarized Milne surface layer yields finite-thickness corrections to the Chandrasekhar solution. We provide compact formulae for the principal and leading subdominant eigenvalues and the asymptotic angular and polarization distributions across both regimes. Combining the recursion with an angle-averaged thermal-Compton redistribution kernel gives approximate energy-resolved Stokes spectra. Comparisons with full polarized Compton calculations show that this separable reconstruction is most reliable for cool, optically thick media. Applied to the non-dipping observations of neutron-star low-mass X-ray binary system 4U 1624-49, the model provides acceptable joint fits to the broadband intensity and IXPE Stokes spectra, showing that an extended corona overlying the accretion disc can account for the observed X-ray polarization.

papers.title: Self-Organizing Maps for the Exploration and Classification of X-Ray Sources in the Chandra Source Catalog
papers.abstract: In this work, we apply Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) to the Chandra Source Catalog (CSC) to investigate the distribution of observation-level detections in the feature space defined by their spectral and variability properties. SOMs are neural-network-based models that project points in high-dimensional space onto a two-dimensional latent space while preserving their local topological structure. From CSC 2.1.1 we extract a sample of 36,904 ACIS-only, observation-level, high statistical significance detections, belonging to 17,927 unique sources. Among these detections, 25,192 (10,078 sources) are associated with a label from SIMBAD via a 1" cross-match that provides information about their astrophysical nature. Training a 40x40 hexagonal SOM reveals structured regions in the U-Matrix and activation response map, and feature-projection maps trace coherent patterns in spectral shape and variability. Overlaying SIMBAD classes shows that labeled populations occupy distinct, partially adjacent regions of the map and that generic categories can be interpreted via their SOM locations. We then retrain the SOM for classification using a source-grouped train/validation/test split and introduce SOMClassifier. When applied to 11,712 detections without SIMBAD labels, it assigns valid (non-abstained) labels to 6,225 detections (coverage ~53%). Furthermore, we release the trained models and visualization/classification workflows through a public web application built on the most up-to-date CSC release.

papers.title: Residual ellipticity driven by intense magnetic stress in the hot neutron star era
papers.abstract: A neutron star with a nonaxisymmetric mass distribution continuously radiates gravitational waves. The amplitude depends on the magnitude of the deformation, and is crucial for gravitational-wave astronomy. We studied an evolutionary effect on the magnetically induced ellipticity in the neutron star crust. A large deformation at the hot era before solidification is assumed to be produced magneto-hydrodynamically, and the fate at later time follows owing to the decrease in the force associated with the decay and redistribution of the current. Instead of simulating the evolution of deformation with the magnetic field over a long timescale, we estimate the ellipticity that remains after the formation of the solid crust by comparing two equilibrium models before and after solidification. The relic ellipticity is $\sim 10^{-8} (B_0/10^{13}{\rm{G}})^2$ in the magnitude for dipole field strength $B_{0}$ at the surface. This value was primarily determined by the magnetic field at the later time, with a weak dependence on the initial large deformation. The memory of the presolidification state was retained, but was small because the elastic force contributes little to the equilibrium.

papers.title: Double Blandford: Resistive GRMHD simulations of accreting black holes simultaneously launch winds and jets
papers.abstract: Magnetic fields can launch outflows through the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) or the Blandford-Payne (BP) mechanism in accreting black hole systems. Despite the dominant launching mechanism still being unclear, the BP process has been insufficiently studied in general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations due to difficulties in generating and maintaining the required large-scale magnetic field geometry. Here, we set up six resistive GRMHD simulations of thin accretion disks with BHAC. The accretion disks in two simulations become magnetically arrested, while the others stay in the standard and normal evolution (SANE) regime. All simulations form jets and winds. The jets are parabolic and collimated by the outer sub-relativistic disk wind; a power law relating the jet width $x$ to the height $z$ as $x\propto z^\mathcal{K}$ yields exponents between 0.52 and 0.64. Among the SANE simulations, the setup with spin parameter $a_* = -0.9375$ has the strongest and most efficient jet, as it accumulates the most magnetic flux at the black hole horizon. For a highly spinning black hole with $a_*=0.9375$, the BZ jet power is $\gtrsim3$ times greater than the disk wind power. The simulated wind regions consist of a highly magnetized region, where the magnetization parameter $\sigma\gg1$, and a less magnetized region. A fast outflow with the potential to reach Lorentz factors up to $\Gamma_\infty\approx25$ propagates in the former region, but because the Lorentz force acts against the disk, it cannot remove a measurable amount of mass from the disk. In the less-magnetized region, a centrifugally driven slower wind efficiently carries away disk material.

papers.title: Bayesian Inference of Fermionic Dark Matter Admixed Neutron Stars Informed by Galaxy Cluster Constraints
papers.abstract: Self-interacting dark matter is constrained on galactic and cluster scales by its elastic scattering cross section per unit mass, $\sigma/m_\chi \sim 0.1-10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. We incorporate this cross section into the equation of state of an asymmetric, self-interacting fermionic dark matter component and perform a Bayesian inference of dark matter admixed neutron stars in the two-fluid framework at $\sigma/m_\chi = 0.1$, $1$ and $10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. Seven nuclear matter parameters are sampled together with the dark particle mass and mass fraction, and confronted with nuclear theory and neutron star observations. The nuclear sector and the global observables are statistically indistinguishable across the whole range of cross sections, while the data constrain the dark matter mass to $m_\chi \simeq 1.45-1.88$~GeV and its mass fraction to $f_\chi \simeq 0.05-0.09$, depending on the cross section. Finally, comparing runs built from the same parameter draws, so that only the cross section differs, we find that it does change the baryonic radius appreciably, but only for light dark matter, a region the astrophysical data largely disfavor. The self-interaction is therefore not too weak to be seen; however its effect is hidden in the region of parameter space that the present observational data already disfavor.

papers.title: The $w$-mode instability of strangeon ergostars and its impact on energy extraction
papers.abstract: Rapidly rotating compact ergostars have been proposed as alternative central engines for short gamma-ray bursts. However, competing energy-loss channels, such as gravitational-wave emission driven by non-axisymmetric instabilities, could curtail the power available for relativistic electromagnetic outflows. In this work, we investigate the $w$-mode instability of rapidly rotating strangeon ergostars by solving the coupled spacetime and fluid perturbation equations in the Hilbert gauge using a spectral method, without relying on a slow-rotation approximation. We calculate the complex eigenvalues of the axial-led and polar-led $w$-mode branches originating from the fundamental $l=m=2$ modes of nonrotating stars along the maximum-energy-extraction paths of twelve representative strangeon equations of state. We find that both branches remain damped throughout these paths, despite the presence of ergoregions. We further vary the stellar angular velocity to determine the instability thresholds. In every case with an identified threshold, the angular velocity at the corresponding extraction-path endpoint remains below the critical value, with the largest ratio being $0.926$. Our results indicate that the $w$-mode instabilities examined here do not provide a growing gravitational-wave emission channel along the considered energy-extraction paths, supporting the availability of the previously estimated rotational energy reservoirs for electromagnetic extraction.

papers.title: Lense-Thirring induced repeating blast trains in continuous gravitational waves
papers.abstract: We characterise gravitational lensing induced by the Lense-Thirring effect in a continuous gravitational-wave source orbiting a spinning supermassive black hole. This scenario is very likely to generate lensing events, as long as the source's orbital inclination is not aligned with the black hole's spin axis and the Lense-Thirring timescale is shorter than the observational window. The signal appears as short-duration ($T_{\rm blast}$) gravitational-wave "blasts" that repeat after every orbit ($T_{\rm orb}$) within a limited time window ($T_{\rm train}$). The blasts' signal strength depends on the system's geometry and not on the black hole mass. The signal will go silent and renew twice in a full Lense-Thirring precession period.

papers.title: A Variable Compact Millimeter Excess in the Type-1 Seyfert Galaxy NGC 985: Implications for a Black-Hole Corona
papers.abstract: Compact millimeter emission from radio-quiet active galactic nuclei has been proposed as a probe of magnetized accretion-disk coronae. We present three epochs of ALMA observations of the type-1 Seyfert galaxy NGC 985, together with archival post-upgrade VLA data presented here for the first time, to investigate its compact millimeter excess. The millimeter flux density decreased strongly between the first two ALMA epochs separated by approximately one month, while the component was detected again at an intermediate level in the third epoch. This variability demonstrates an intrinsically variable compact component and implies a model-independent size limit of $\lesssim 0.024$ pc ($\simeq 1.1\times10^3 R_{\rm S}$). Spectral decomposition requires a compact, self-absorbed synchrotron component to reproduce the millimeter-wave data. A hybrid thermal/nonthermal coronal model reproduces the radio-millimeter spectra, with the two broadly sampled ALMA epochs favoring different nonthermal electron distributions. The estimated radiative cooling times are comparable to or shorter than the light-crossing time, implying continuous injection or reacceleration of nonthermal electrons; a change in particle injection is the most natural driver of the observed spectral changes. We conclude that NGC 985 hosts a recurrent and variable compact millimeter synchrotron component. A magnetized corona provides a plausible origin, although the present data do not uniquely distinguish a coronal origin from alternatives such as a jet base.

papers.title: Joint Bayesian Inference of Dense Matter and f(Q) Gravity with Nuclear and Neutron Star Constraints
papers.abstract: We investigate neutron star (NS) properties in symmetric teleparallel $f(Q)$ gravity while consistently accounting for uncertainties in the dense matter equation of state (EOS). We focus on the linear $f(Q)$ model and perform a joint Bayesian inference of the nuclear matter and modified gravity parameters using a Taylor expansion EOS around nuclear saturation density. The analysis incorporates complementary constraints from nuclear saturation properties, chiral effective field theory calculations of pure neutron matter, heavy-ion collision, and empirical nuclear data, the GW170817 tidal deformability posterior, and NICER mass--radius measurements. The resulting posterior distributions simultaneously constrain the dense matter and gravity sectors and quantify their correlations within a common framework. For a canonical $1.4\,M_\odot$ NS, we obtain $R_{1.4}=11.28^{+0.35}_{-0.31}\,\mathrm{km}$ and $\Lambda_{1.4}=151.4^{+44.9}_{-31.2}$, while the maximum mass is constrained to $M_{\rm max}=2.22^{+0.29}_{-0.16}\,M_\odot$. The modified gravity parameters exhibit only weak direct correlations with most stellar observables, while a pronounced degeneracy remains within the gravity sector. Our results show that accounting for EOS uncertainties is essential for quantifying the interplay between dense matter physics and modified gravity and provide a systematic framework for confronting symmetric teleparallel gravity with nuclear and multimessenger NS observations.

papers.title: SuSy and CoDy Radiation from Evaporating Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay between physics beyond the Standard Model and modified spacetime geometries in shaping the photon and neutrino spectra from evaporating black holes. We implement three representative supersymmetric (SuSy) benchmarks and a composite dynamics (CoDy) scenario in BlackHawk. We consider both Schwarzschild black holes and regular black holes geometries, namely polymerized, Hayward, and Simpson--Visser black holes. New degrees of freedom at the TeV scale become accessible at Hawking temperatures corresponding to black hole masses of approximately $M_{\rm BH}\sim 10^{10}\,\mathrm{g}$. We show that physics beyond the Standard Model produces distinctive signatures in both the instantaneous secondary-photon and neutrino spectra. Radiative decays generate narrow spectral features with approximately temperature-independent relative amplitudes, while multistep decay cascades produce broad enhancements that become increasingly pronounced at higher temperatures. In contrast, compressed mass spectra exhibit no localized features. Crucially, we show that the effects of new particle physics and modified spacetime geometries can become intertwined in specific energy regimes, altering the resulting spectral signatures. Our results demonstrate that photon and neutrino spectra provide complementary probes of new particle physics and black hole geometry, with predicted spectral enhancements extending into the energy ranges accessible to current and future high-energy observatories.

papers.title: Spins do not add: why rotating stars do not help spin-up black holes in binaries
papers.abstract: It is well-known that in the merger of a black-hole binary with spins aligned with the orbital angular momentum, the spin of the final black hole always increases with the spin of the components. We show that this very intuitive behavior is violated in black hole--neutron star binaries, where the spin of the final black hole actually decreases as the spin of the neutron star increases. Using a large set of binaries with different spins and mass ratios, we identify the mechanism behind this surprising result in the nonlinear dynamics of the tidal disruption, which drives a substantial loss of angular momentum via dynamical ejecta, in some cases comparable to that radiated via gravitational waves. Our results highlight that the spin evolution of stellar-mass black holes involved in binary mergers is different from what normally assumed, far more complex, and interesting.

papers.title: Early-Excess SNe Ia Show Strong C II Absorption
papers.abstract: Some type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) exhibit an early excess in their rising light curves, but the physical origin of this behavior remains uncertain. The processes driving these excesses affect the ejecta at early times and may also imprint on the outermost layers. We investigate whether early excesses are associated with differences in unburned material by measuring pre-maximum carbon absorption. Using multi-component Gaussian fits to the blended Si II $\lambda6355$ and C II $\lambda6580$ region, we measure pseudo-equivalent widths and velocities for a sample of 35 nonpeculiar SNe Ia with rising light curve categorizations. We find that early-excess objects ($n=13$) tend to exhibit stronger C II absorption than non-excesses ($n=22$) at phases earlier than approximately $-13$ d, with a two-sample K-S test of the earliest measurements yielding $p=0.025$. In contrast, the HV Si II components do not clearly separate the two groups. Early-excess SNe Ia tend to be more luminous and decline more slowly, but objects with similar maximum-light properties span a range of C II pseudo-equivalent widths, suggesting that this effect is distinct from the known luminosity-width relation. We show that, at least in some cases, when objects have similar light-curve shape and photospheric temperature, the effect we see is not driven by ionization but by distinct differences in the explosion, such as carbon abundance and density and the efficiency of burning in the WD. Our results provide a new constraint on SN Ia explosion models for early excesses, as they must produce a tendency for stronger early C II absorption.

papers.title: New Physics in Ultra-High-Energy Neutrino Flavor
papers.abstract: Neutrino flavor measurements test physics beyond the Standard Model that modifies neutrino production, propagation, or detection. IceCube has measured the flavor composition of the astrophysical neutrino flux up to PeV energies. Next-generation experiments will extend flavor measurements to the ultra-high-energy (UHE) regime, $100\,\mathrm{PeV}$-$10\,\mathrm{EeV}$, by combining in-ice radio detection with Earth-skimming tau neutrinos. We present the first study of the new-physics reach of these projected UHE flavor measurements. We take Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) as a benchmark, since its effects grow as a power of the neutrino energy. We find that UHE flavor ratios will be the most sensitive probe of LIV for operators of dimension four and higher, improving on current bounds from all sectors by up to twenty orders of magnitude. Three-flavor observables improve this sensitivity by up to an order of magnitude over Earth-skimming tau neutrinos alone.

papers.title: Post-adiabatic effects sourced by radiation reaction for inspiraling, eccentric binaries in post-Newtonian theory
papers.abstract: The adiabatic approximation, in which eccentric binaries evolve under orbit-averaged fluxes, is widely used in gravitational-wave and astrophysical modeling. We use resummed multiple-scale analysis, which is closely related to near-identity averaging transformations, to derive post-adiabatic corrections from leading-order radiation reaction and explain how the accuracy of the adiabatic approximation depends on the initial orbital phase. While the secular evolution equations for the eccentricity and semi-major axis receive no explicit first post-adiabatic corrections, their solutions acquire such corrections through the initial conditions. We also derive the change in the functional form of the gravitational-wave polarizations that cancels the gauge dependence of the orbital elements at first post-adiabatic order, ensuring agreement between waveforms evaluated at the same physical event in different coordinates. At a radial turning point, the first post-adiabatic oscillations of the semi-major axis and eccentricity vanish, so the initial osculating energy and angular momentum agree with their orbit-averaged values up to second post-adiabatic corrections. When initialized elsewhere along the orbit, the adiabatic approximation can accumulate significant dephasing, which the first post-adiabatic approximation can substantially reduce. Both dephasings can change sign across parameter space, consistent with competing contributions from successive orders. Accounting for initialization is therefore essential for assessing the accuracy of these approximations, particularly for long-lived, highly eccentric binaries.

papers.title: Prospects for probing supermassive binary black holes in strongly lensed active galactic nuclei via microlensing effects
papers.abstract: Gravitational microlensing in strongly lensed active galactic nuclei (AGNs) provides a powerful probe of accretion-disk structure and may offer a unique opportunity to identify sub-parsec supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) through distinctive signatures. Upcoming wide-field surveys are expected to discover a large sample of strongly lensed AGNs, a fraction of which may host SMBBHs detectable via microlensing. In this paper, we employ semi-analytic models to assess the detection prospects of sub-parsec SMBBHs in lensed AGNs, focusing on systems with resolvable multiple images suitable for microlensing analysis. Accounting for galaxy-scale strong-lensing statistics, and including the cluster-lensing contribution as an optimistic statistical extension, we estimate that up to approximately 87 such systems could be spatially resolved by individual upcoming surveys, including the Vera C. Rubin Observatory (Rubin), Euclid, China's Space Survey Telescope (CSST), and the Roman. For the Rubin WFD survey, we estimate that periodic oscillations in microlensing light curves could identify $\sim0.12-0.68$ short-period ($<5$\,yr) binaries, whereas diagnostics based on the reconstructed size-wavelength relation apply to a broader population, potentially identifying $\sim0.4-5.3$ systems, depending on the model assumptions. CSST, Euclid, and Roman may also reveal up to $10.6$, $8.9$, and $1.2$ systems exhibiting size-wavelength features, and $2.3$, $1.9$, $0.3$ systems showing periodic oscillations, which should be regarded as imaging-selected candidates whose microlensing-based identification requires adequate time-domain follow-up, including cadence, monitoring baseline, photometric precision, and reliable time-delay measurements. Our results show that strongly lensed AGNs provide a promising, though observationally demanding, pathway for finding candidate SMBBHs via microlensing.

papers.title: Non-Gaussian matter fluctuations from primordial magnetic fields and galaxy luminosity function
papers.abstract: Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) represent a promising candidate for the origin of large-scale magnetic fields observed in astrophysical environments. Through the Lorentz force, PMFs generate matter density perturbations, leaving distinct imprints on the formation of cosmic structures. While previous studies have primarily characterized these imprints via the matter power spectrum --- a two-point statistic --- we demonstrate that the one-point statistics of PMF-induced density fluctuations reveal an intrinsically non-Gaussian probability distribution function (PDF), even when the PMFs themselves are statistically Gaussian. In particular, we find that the high-density tail of the PDF is enhanced by over two orders of magnitude relative to the Gaussian case. Adopting the Press-Schechter formalism, we show that this non-Gaussianity significantly boosts the abundance of rare objects, especially massive halos and those at high redshifts. We further compute the ultraviolet luminosity function of galaxies at $z=6$, $12$, and $16$, and compare our predictions with recent James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations that have reported an excess of high-redshift galaxies at $z\sim 12$ -- $16$ relative to standard $\Lambda$CDM expectations. Intriguingly, in the limiting case where the total density field inherits this PDF, our results suggest that the non-Gaussian density fluctuations sourced by PMFs can explain the bright-end ($M_\mathrm{UV}\lesssim -18$) excess at $z\gtrsim 12$, without requiring additional astrophysical enhancements to star-formation efficiency.

papers.title: Enhancing Graviton--Photon Conversion through Galactic Magnetic Turbulence
papers.abstract: Plasma dispersion suppresses coherent graviton-photon conversion over astrophysical distances. We show that Galactic magnetic turbulence enables phase matching by compensating the plasma-induced mismatch, allowing matched magnetic modes to contribute coherently. In the long path limit, the ensemble-averaged conversion probability grows linearly with propagation distance in the phase matched regime and is governed by the projected magnetic power spectrum. Applied to photon background observations, this mechanism yields characteristic strain limits that are stronger than previous Galactic conversion bounds in the inertial range phase matching window, with improvements of up to two orders of magnitude.

papers.title: FOORT: Flexible Object-Oriented Ray Tracing
papers.abstract: We present FOORT (Flexible Object-Oriented Ray Tracing), an open C++ code for ray-tracing images of black holes and other compact objects in arbitrary spacetimes. FOORT is designed to offer flexibility and can handle horizons, naked singularities and numerical metrics, allowing it to ray-trace numerous different metrics including Kerr and other black holes, as well as horizonless objects such as fuzzballs and boson stars. New metrics, analytical or numerical, can be added with minimal effort, and geodesics are initialized at the camera without reference to conserved quantities, so no special structure of the metric is required. Besides the intensity observed from a geometrically and optically thin equatorial disk, FOORT is set up to track a number of diagnostics along each geodesic, such as the number of equatorial crossings and the radius of closest approach. Its adaptive mesh can refine the image on any of these diagnostics, efficiently resolving narrow features such as higher-order photon rings. Accompanying Python tools convert the output into images and interferometric visibility amplitudes. We describe the main features of the code, validate it against analytic results in the Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes, demonstrate it on several non-Kerr metrics, and characterize its scaling with the number of OpenMP threads. FOORT is lightweight, requiring only C++17 and OpenMP, and has already been used in a number of studies of black hole and compact-object imaging. The code is publicly available in a GitHub repository.

papers.title: A unified mean-field description of dense hadron matter constrained from $\chi$EFT and lattice QCD
papers.abstract: We construct a relativistic mean field theory (RMFT) of hadrons in an attempt to describe the confined phase of QCD across a wide range of temperatures and baryon densities. This includes the scalar and vector mesons interacting with baryons and resonances up to $3$ GeV, including those which are not yet discovered but predicted within the quark model and lattice QCD. The baryon--meson couplings are constrained through a two-stage Bayesian analysis. In the first stage, we constrain six different couplings in our theory using six nuclear empirical parameters inferred from the chiral effective field theory predictions of the energy per nucleon for pure neutron matter over baryon densities $n_B \in [0.08, 0.32]~\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$, employing a Gaussian-process likelihood to account for correlations in the input data. In the second stage, this posterior is set as the prior for constraining different baryon--meson couplings in our RMFT construction, using lattice QCD input. The resulting posterior provides substantially improved constraints for different baryon--meson couplings and non-linear meson self-interactions, which are consistent with the current astrophysical observations of neutron star masses, radii and tidal deformability parameters.

papers.title: Exact model of a gravitational wave and electromagnetic radiation in DHOST gravity theory: wave solutions and testable effects
papers.abstract: Within an analytical non-perturbative framework based on a single exact model, the coupled dynamics of gravitational waves and high-frequency electromagnetic fields is investigated in General Relativity and DHOST gravity. Using an exact gravitational-wave spacetime in an isotropic (null) wave coordinate system, Maxwell's equations are integrated analytically. This analysis provides an exact non-perturbative confirmation from the full field equations that a gravitational wave acts as a waveguide, forming a propagation channel for electromagnetic radiation co-directional with the gravitational wave and generating an effective pure-radiation source. Applying this exact electrodynamic solution to the nonlinear field equations of DHOST class~Ia gravity reveals that the algebraic structure of the DHOST constraint equations enforces a modification of the electromagnetic-wave parameters. Based on this mechanism, an observationally testable effect of scalar frequency drift is derived, providing a direct way to discriminate between General Relativity and modified gravity theories even when their metric tensors share identical functional forms.

papers.title: Slow Macroscopic Rotations of Neutron Stars With a Deformed Effective Surface
papers.abstract: The macroscopic model for a neutron star (NS) as a finite perfect fluid at the equilibrium is extended to rotating deformed systems by incorporating the linear perturbation expansion over a small frequency $\omega$ near the Schwarzschild gravitational metric within the effective-surface (ES) approach. The NS angular momentum $I$ and moment of inertia (MI) for a slow stationary azimuthal rotation around the symmetry axis is calculated by using the Kerr metric approach in spheroidal coordinates, and compared with the spherical results. The gradient surface terms of the macroscopic NS energy density $\mathcal{E}(\rho)$ (Equation of State) are taken into account along with the volume ones at the leading order of the leptodermic parameter $a/R \ll 1$, where $a$ is the ES crust thickness and $R$ is the NS effective radius. The analytical macroscopic NS MI expressions, $\Theta = dI/d\omega = \widetilde{\Theta}/(1-\mathcal{T}_{t\varphi})$, have been obtained in terms of the statistically averaged MI, $\tilde{\Theta}$, and its time and azimuthal-angle $t,\varphi$ correlation, $\mathcal{T}_{t\varphi}$, as sums of the volume and surface components. The MI $\Theta$ is changed significantly as function of the effective radius $R$ and deformation parameter because of a strong gravity. We found the additional narrower constraints for the NS radius due mainly to the $t,\varphi$ correlations and surface contributions and NS surface deformation.
